variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
let immutable = "Constant"
let mutable mut = 42
mut <- 43
variables.notes: F# values are immutable by default. Mutation requires 'mutable' and '<-' operator.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
let i: int = 1
let d: float = 1.0
let b: bool = true
let s: string = "Text"
let opt: int option = Some 42
data_types.notes: Option types are used instead of nulls.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
let sum = 1 + 2
let eq = 1 = 1
let piped = 5 |> add 2
operators.notes: Equality is '=', not '=='. The pipe operator '|>' is heavily used to chain operations.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
let max = if a > b then a else b

let typeName = match x with
    | 1 -> "One"
    | n when n < 10 -> "Small"
    | _ -> "Other"
conditionals.notes: Pattern matching is a core feature for control flow.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.code:
for i in 1 .. 5 do printfn "%d" i

let doubled = [ for x in 1..3 -> x * 2 ]
for_loop.notes: List/Array comprehensions are used to generate new collections.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.notes: While loops are used mostly for mutable imperative code.

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
let add a b = a + b

let multiply = fun a b -> a * b
functions.notes: Functions are automatically curried. 'let' is used to define both values and functions.

maps.title: Maps
maps.notes: Maps are immutable. Adding an item returns a new Map.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: Idiomatic F# often uses Result<'T, 'Error> types instead of exceptions.

comments.title: Comments & Documentation
comments.notes: F# provides comments to document code behavior.

numbers.title: Numbers & Constants
numbers.notes: F# supports numeric literals for computation and indexing.

booleans.title: Booleans & Conditions
booleans.notes: F# provides boolean conditions for program control flow.

type_casting.title: Type Conversion
type_casting.notes: F# converts data between native format representations.

strings.title: Strings & Characters
strings.notes: F# represents textual data through string literals and character arrays.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: F# formats and joins textual values for display and output.

pattern_matching.title: Conditionals & Branching
pattern_matching.code:
case value of
    1: execute_one()
    default: execute_default()
pattern_matching.notes: F# branches execution based on value comparison and conditional expressions.

range.title: Ranges & Intervals
range.notes: F# defines intervals and index sequences for bounded processing.

iterators.title: Iteration & Loops
iterators.notes: F# iterates across collections and sequence elements.

oop_classes.title: Structures & Modules
oop_classes.notes: F# organizes data and behavior through structures or modular components.

lists.title: Collections & Arrays
lists.notes: F# stores sequence data in indexed lists or arrays.

tuples.title: Records & Pairs
tuples.notes: F# groups related fields into lightweight composite pairs or records.

sets.title: Sets & Uniqueness
sets.notes: F# tracks unique values without duplicate entries.

modules_import.title: Libraries & Modules
modules_import.notes: F# organizes external libraries and code units into modular namespaces.
